title: license show
description: What <app> license show answers with -o json, on envelope/v2, for licenses of elderlygate/mankit/license/v2 (license-payload.schema.json): the app's license state and whether it warns, whether this build is a release, every license it took with the one active for this app marked, its trial, the files it refused, and every feature in its feature state with where it is unlocked from, so the CLI, its JSON, the top bar's badge and the License group on the app's Settings page show the same answer and none of them works anything out (ADR-L3, L8, L9). mankit's license check makes it for every app, so every app answers it alike. mankit/v2's LicenseShow is the answer before it.

data.description: The app's license state and warn, its build, the licenses it took, its trial, the files it refused, the counts and its features.

state.description: What the badge and the License group say, one word for the license state of the whole app (ADR-L3), worked out here once; whether the build is a release is build's alone to say. The first of these that holds decides it. licensed: the active license has not ended, has begun and, when it names lines, names this build's line (ADR-L10, V-10). trial: the trial runs (trial, ADR-L9). free: anything else, so use is free (ADR-L3): no active license, or one not begun yet, ended, broken or not naming this build's line, and no trial, or one ended. The app never takes another license by itself when the active one does not run (ADR-L8).

endedOn.description: The active license's last day, when state is free and that license has ended, so ADR-L3's notice names the day and a page never picks a license. Absent otherwise.

sentence.description: The one sentence a reader shows for the app's license state, made by mankit's license check and shown word for word: readers never build or change it, so the CLI, the web badge and panel and the TUI say the same. Present when the state has one: a running trial, with its days left and last day; an ended trial; licensed, naming whom the active license is for; and an active license that has ended or is broken, saying why the app runs on its trial or free (ADR-L8). Absent otherwise. Its words are the license check's to choose.

warn.description: True when a reader shows the license state in its warn colour; the answer decides and readers never do (ADR-L3). True when state is licensed and the active license is in the warning ADR-L3's built-in threshold license-expiring sets; when state is trial and the trial is in its last days, as that threshold counts them; and when state is free and the trial or the active license has ended, until it is replaced or removed (ADR-L3). Absent or false otherwise, so a license that never ends never warns.

licenses.description: Every license file the app read and took: the org licenses that name it and its own (ADR-L8), at most one of them active. The trial is not a license and is in trial instead (ADR-L9). While mankit still reads mankit/v1's files, an org or product file shows as a license here (ADR-L8). A file it refused is in refused instead, never here. Empty when there is none, so a reader tells no license from a failure.

refused.description: Every license file the app read but did not take, so a refused file never shows as a license and a person sees why (ADR-L1, L5, L6, L8, L9). Its reason is one of signature, untrusted_key, other_build, unreadable, wrong_place, id_mismatch and retired_kind, each meaning what problem/v1's reason says. Empty when none was refused.

features.description: Every feature of the app, in the order its feature list gives them: its feature state and where it is unlocked from, so the License group draws this answer alone (ADR-L2, L8).

allOf.description: A day a license ended is named only while use is free, and it always warns.
Licensed means the active license is listed and has not ended.
A trial state means the trial is listed and has not ended.
A running trial means the state is trial, never free.
A day a license ended names a license that is active and has ended.

license.description: One license file the app read: its id and place, whom it names, what it opens or until when, the key that signed it, and whether it is the app's active one. Every one is of the payload's one kind, license (license-payload.schema.json), so it names no kind.

id.description: The license's id, as its signed payload says: the one a user names in license use <id> and license remove <id> (ADR-L8).

place.description: Where the license file sits (ADR-L8; the paths: the mankit README). org: the org's licenses folder, shared by every app; app: this app's own licenses folder. So a reader shows whose a license is, and license remove knows which file it removes.

for.description: Whom the license names, as its signed payload says.

lines.description: The product lines it opens, as its signed payload says, so a reader shows a license that never ends by what it opens. Absent when the payload names none.

issued.description: The license's first day, as its signed payload says, so a reader shows a license not begun yet.

until.description: The license's last day, as its signed payload says.

daysLeft.description: The days left until the license's last day, until, 0 once it has ended. Absent when the license never ends. license check gives only this; when to warn is the threshold's to say (ADR-L3).

ended.description: True once the license's last day, until, has passed: its features are locked again, and what they made stays readable (ADR-L3). Always false for a license that never ends.

active.description: True on the app's active license, the one its features and state rest on, and on at most one license (ADR-L8). It is the one license use or license add chose in this app; with no choice made, it is the newest license that names the app (ADR-L8); other apps keep their own choice. Still true when it has ended or does not name this build's line, as the app never switches to another license by itself. When the chosen file is refused, none here is true and sentence says why.

allOf.description: An ended license has no days left.
A license meets its payload's rule: it either runs until a day or names the lines it opens, never both (license-payload.schema.json).
A license with a last day counts its days left to it; one that never ends has none and never ends.

trial.description: The app's trial, a rule in mankit and not a license: every enterprise feature of the app for ADR-L9's trial length from its first start, for the product line stamped in its build, with nothing signed (ADR-L9). When it started is the trial note's to say (trial-started.schema.json). Absent when the app has no trial, as on its first start it held a license and wrote no note.

until.description: The trial's last day: the note's day plus ADR-L9's trial length, less one, as the first day counts, so a reader shows when it ends.

daysLeft.description: The days left until the trial's last day, 0 once it has ended. license check gives only this; when to warn is the threshold's to say (ADR-L3).

ended.description: True once the trial's last day has passed: the features it opened are locked again, and what they made stays readable (ADR-L3).

allOf.description: An ended trial has no days left.

window.description: The countdown the License group's bar shows, present only while one shows: a running trial (ADR-L9), or a license in the warning the threshold of ADR-L3 sets. Its days left are daysLeft beside it.

of.description: The countdown's whole length in days: ADR-L9's trial length, or the warning window mankit reads from the threshold (ADR-L3), so the bar shows daysLeft out of it.

feature.description: One feature of the app: its feature state, each field as mankit/v1 defs' featureState says, and where it is unlocked from, a row of the License group's features table (ADR-L8).

from.description: Where the feature is unlocked from, worked out with state (ADR-L8, L9). license: the active license runs and names it; trial: the active license does not run or does not name it, and the trial runs; none: nothing opens it, as a free feature needs nothing and an enterprise feature with none is locked.

until.description: The last day the feature stays open, an RFC 3339 date: the last day of what unlocks it, the active license's until or the trial's until. Absent when from is none, and when an active license that never ends opens it.

allOf.description: featureState's own rules hold here too.
A feature nothing opens has no last day.
A feature a trial opens stays open until the trial ends.
A license names enterprise features only, and a trial opens only those, so a free feature is never unlocked from one (ADR-L2, L9).

day.description: A day, an RFC 3339 date in UTC: the one form every day in this answer takes.
